title: 10,000 tiny PyTorch kernels in eager mode
job: A Python loop of 10,000 in-place adds on a one-element fp32 CUDA tensor (x.add_(1.0)) in PyTorch eager mode, then one synchronize: the shape of an unfused optimizer step or a small-batch decode loop.
derivation: launches = 10,000: one elementwise kernel per add_ (checked with torch.profiler)

observation.tool: PyTorch torch.utils.benchmark.Timer around the loop; torch.profiler for the kernel count
observation.metric: median wall time of the whole 10,000-op loop including the final synchronize

tolerance.why: The launch constant is napkin-bench's back-to-back empty-kernel launch through the CUDA driver API from Rust, not a framework op. The model has no term for per-op framework overhead (Python, the PyTorch dispatcher, tensor checks), so a framework loop is expected to be slower than predicted. A factor of 2 is the widest error at which a launch-bound estimate still sizes the job usefully; outside it the model is missing a term, which this case is meant to expose.

match: one kernel launch per op, confirmed by the profiler's kernel count
excludes: per-op host overhead of Python and the PyTorch dispatcher
the caching allocator: no allocations happen inside the loop
CUDA graphs and kernel fusion, which would remove launches
